summary: Misallocated trial credits charged to parent org after customer split their sub-orgs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that multiple trial credits which should have been applied to newly created sub-organizations were instead deducted from the parent billing account after a recent org-split operation. The customer was invoiced for usage that should have been covered by the trial credits.

Impact:
- Immediate invoice charge for $13,420 on billing cycle 2026-02-28 despite existing trial credits assigned to their account.
- Customer-facing outage: finance team blocked from approving new capacity purchases while dispute is open; potential churn risk.

Environment:
- Production (us-east) billing pipeline; affected billing ledger entries span 2026-02-25 to 2026-02-28.

Steps to reproduce / observed behavior:
1) Customer performed an org split on 2026-02-24 to create two sub-orgs under the same billing account.
2) Trial credits were visible in the UI on the new sub-orgs but were not associated in the billing ledger.
3) End of month metering ran on 2026-02-28 and charged usage against the parent orgId (billing_id: BILL-ACME-001).
4) Billing export shows credits applied to parent ledger line items rather than to sub-org usage lines.

Logs/IDs/Artifacts:
- Billing ledger lines: BL-89234, BL-89235, BL-89236
- Org split audit: AUD-20260224-778
- Customer invoice: INV-2026-02-28-ACME-01
- Slack thread: #support (thread ts: 1677321000.000200)

Requested outcome from customer: restore credits to the intended sub-orgs and issue a corrected invoice or credit memo.
investigation_notes:
Initial triage (2026-03-03): support confirmed invoice and ledger lines. Billing team (Marta Gomez) reviewed allocation codepath in billing-allocator service. Hypothesis: race condition during org-split where 'primary_billing_entity' flag was temporarily null for sub-orgs, causing credits to fall back to parent.

Actions performed:
- Pulled billing export for invoice INV-2026-02-28-ACME-01 and correlated usage tokens to ledger lines BL-89234..BL-89236.
- Replayed allocation logic locally against test fixture reproducing org-split sequence (found credits assigned to parent when billing_entity_id null).
- Identified offending code: billing-allocator v1.8.2 that uses a tolerant join and defaults to parent id on null.
- Created PR with fix to ensure atomic assignment during org creation: github.com/redwood-inference/platform/pull/5123.

Interim mitigation:
- Manually adjusted accounting entries for Acme: created temporary credit memo CM-2026-03-04-ACME to offset parent invoice until fix is deployed.
resolution:
Temporary resolution (2026-03-05): issued credit memo CM-2026-03-04-ACME for $13,420 against INV-2026-02-28-ACME-01 and applied corrective ledger entries so the customer's parent invoice balances to zero. Confirmed with customer that credits now appear in sub-org UI balances.

Permanent fix: billing-allocator PR merged and scheduled for release in 2026-03-06 deploy window (PR 5123). Post-deploy test plan to run org-split scenarios and end-of-month metering on a staging fixture.

Follow-ups:
- Billing team to run a sweep for other org-splits in the last 30 days (task INT-4125).
- Proactive outreach to customers with recent org-splits to verify credit allocations.
